designBreaks.attack: Cross-prompt anchor plus per-turn injected messages that never enter working memory. Examples: @file mention injection (default-ON, up to 256 KiB), hook-context and context-change messages, and the trailing system-reminder (memory, skills, working state). R1 hashes a digest over the wm prefix, so after the next user prompt the digest still matches. But the provider count P included the injected content from the previous prompt, which is no longer sent.
designBreaks.bypassOrRegression: REGRESSION introduced by the fix: occupancy is over-counted by the size of the vanished injection, which causes premature, lossy compaction. Today, round 1 of prompt 2 undercounts by about 9.3k. Under R1 it overcounts by 50k. The digest cannot detect this because the injected content is not in wm. Hashing the sent messages instead would not help either: the trailing reminder sits at the tail of every request, so the anchor would never be valid.
designBreaks.evidence: Probe a1-mention-ephemeral.ts (real runAgent, mentionInjector returns 200k chars when the prompt contains @big). Prompt 1 sent providerInput 109351; the wm does not contain the mention (wm_contains_big false). Prompt 2 round 1 actual sent 59390. R1's anchored formula P + est(suffix) = 109390, so r1_overcount_tokens = 50000. Code: the mention is re-resolved from the latest user text every round and never stored (context-assembler.ts:147-169, :553-575). compile() appends injected messages after baseMessages and pushes the trailing reminder (prompt.ts:766-770, 796-815). @file is default-ON (host/runtime/agent-config-assembler.ts:715; mention-wire.ts:53-80; base.ts:20).

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: (1) Under QUANTA_LLM_REPLAY the port has no model, so 200k, 25% and 123k are unreachable (probe a4). The implementer will have to rewrite the expectations, most likely to whatever the code prints. (2) formatTokens shows values of 100k and above as whole k (status-line.ts:23-28), so the 'estimated suffix' is invisible: a mutation that drops the suffix estimate stays green. (3) Its only realistic control uses inputTokens 2000 against a real CLI prefix of about 9.5k or more, a state no provider produces. (4) R1 admits the test was never run.
jankyTests.fix: Forward opts.model and contextWindowKey into the replay port (factory.ts replay branch via forwardPortIdentity) and assert that seam first. Choose a suffix large enough to cross a displayed k boundary (e.g. a 6k-char assistant reply), so removing the suffix changes the rendered head. Add a control where the anchor comes from a request that contained an @file and the next prompt has none.

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: (1) Round 2's expected value uses fixed(inputs[1]) and messages from llm.inputs[1] inside a preflight spy that fires before inputs[1] exists (probe a1 order). The set-difference 'messages not present in inputs[0]' is undefined for the per-turn reminder. As specified it cannot be implemented. (2) The round 1 expectation is computed with the same exported occupancy estimator, so it is a tautology and blind to the injected channel (50k miss, probe a1). (3) Mutation (3), visibleSpecs vs all specs, is a no-op without an armed skill gate or plan mode: filterSpecsByScope returns the same array (skill-gate.ts:55-57). (4) The paired control ('below 90% of 123k', spy never called) sits at 89% with defaultTools alone (probe a5: 109,461 tokens); the larger real CLI registry tips it over, so the control depends on registry size.
jankyTests.fix: Assert at the send seam (onTurnStreamInput tap) that reading.totalTokens equals an independent chars/4 over the recorded request bytes (system + tools JSON + all sent messages) for unanchored rounds. Pin the display-vs-trigger identity separately. Arm plan mode or a skill scope when running mutation (3). Size the control history so the margin from both ratios is at least 10%, computed from the recorded request rather than hand arithmetic.

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: Every scenario uses plain-text prompts, so the regression where the anchor includes an injected message that is gone on the next prompt stays green (probe a1: +50,000). The formula is written against 'recorded inputs' without separating wm content from injected content.
jankyTests.fix: Add the paired case: turn 1 contains @file, which the real CLI mention wire injects, and turn 2 does not. Assert round 1 of turn 2 is within the injected-size-free estimate of the recorded request, i.e. not P + suffix.

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: No runtime SSOT for LlmSurfaceId exists, so the 'both directions' guard compares two hand lists. There is also no case for a usage payload without a prompt-side count.
jankyTests.fix: Turn LlmSurfaceId into `export const LLM_SURFACE_IDS = [...] as const` and derive the type from it; the guard reads that const. Add adapter cases (Anthropic message_start without input_tokens; Responses usage without input_tokens) that must yield 'prompt count absent', not 0.

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: (c) pins 'accept any provider count', with no control for inputTokens 0 or absent, so the fail-open in probe a2 would be locked in as correct. (e) asserts sum(categories) === total alongside a clamped residual, which cannot both hold.
jankyTests.fix: Split (c) into 'provider count below the estimate is accepted' and 'absent or zero prompt count never anchors' (paired). Define the clamped-case invariant explicitly (e.g. categories scaled, or a sum-exceeds-total flag rendered).

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: It asserts compactThresholdTokens 123000 on a surface R1 itself recommends marking autoCompaction:false. It relies on the replay port's model (probe a4). The 'exact frame count per ledger publish' has no defined publish semantics (recordSend, captureUsage, measure).

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: Hand-built frames only. Nothing binds them to what the daemon serializes (the canvas mirror is hand-maintained and has no drift test), so the test stays green if the daemon never sends source. It also skips the StatusBar warning and category-hues.
jankyTests.fix: Generate the canvas ContextUsageMessage type the same way the session protocol is generated, or add a drift-contract test over src/protocol/canvas/messages.ts. Feed the frontend adapter a frame captured from the H7 daemon run. Cover lib/context-warning.ts and category-hues.

jankyTests.whyVacuousOrWeak: The '.inputTokens/.cacheReadTokens property reads' rule is name matching, not type resolution: 96 production reads fall outside src/llm and usage-accounting, e.g. side-conversation UsageTally. With 87 estimateTokens references across 21 files, it needs about 200 site keys built on (file, enclosing function), a key known to go stale. It cannot see arithmetic re-derivations such as apps/web-frontend/src/lib/context-warning.ts (probe a3), which is exactly the second computation that exists today.
jankyTests.fix: Make re-derivation hard by type, not by allowlist. Render functions accept only the branded ContextOccupancy (or a projection whose constructor is module-private) and receive pre-computed percent and warn-level fields, so a frontend never divides total by max itself. Keep a small census of only the brand constructor and resolveOccupancyWindow call sites.

overEngineeringOrHeuristics: The side ledger (sha256 prefix chain, WeakMap memo, attach/detach, observeTranscript host seam, deferred resume-persistence packet) re-implements what the transcript can carry. quanta already has local-only message metadata that is never sent to adapters (Message.id and provenance, src/llm/types.ts:11-40). Claude Code stores provider usage on the assistant message and walks back to it (chunk-3j0en1hg.js:106359-106399, Wm/ALn). A usage anchor on the message would travel with host history, resume, rewind and forks for free, with no mutable session slot for config spreads to inherit. The digest can stay as a field on that anchor.

USAGE_CONVENTION_BY_SURFACE as Record<LlmSurfaceId, Provider> plus a runtime 'drift guard' is ceremony without a runtime SSOT (LlmSurfaceId is type-only, llm-route-types.ts:5). The simpler structural move is to have the adapter emit disjoint buckets, or an explicit promptTokens that may be undefined, at the boundary where the grammar is known. That also makes the missing-count case in probe a2 representable instead of 0.

'Compaction buffer' and 'Free space' as category rows mix non-occupancy quantities into segments. That breaks the sum-to-total invariant used by the CLI cell allocator (status-line.ts:153-157), web share math (slash-context-gauge.ts:50-56) and the string-keyed hue map (category-hues.ts:26-34). Render them as separate head annotations.

The residualClamped flag and 'Messages = total − estimated fixed' residual hide estimator error inside the one category users care about. It is honest only if the frame also ships fixedEstimate vs providerTokens, which R1's H5 does not require.

WeakMap memo 'per message object': if it caches chain values rather than per-message content hashes, message objects reused at new positions after compaction (the kept suffix after a summary) return the old chain digest, and a stale anchor validates. R1 says 'correctness does not depend on identity', which holds only for per-message hashing. The design does not specify which. UNVERIFIED because nothing is implemented yet.

The rollout's measurement receipt (SWE-bench 6-pick + loop-d4-d5) is presented as evidence, but single-run bench instances without a mention wire cannot exercise the cross-prompt anchor or the injected-message channel, so it would be a ceremonial receipt (runner/batch/eval/driver/context-types.ts:104-116; config-build.ts:623).
